content.title: About
content.content: A meat taco without cheese is a classic Mexican snack consisting of a soft or crispy tortilla filled with seasoned ground meat, fresh vegetables, and spices. The absence of cheese makes it lighter and suitable for those avoiding dairy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The word “taco” comes from Spanish, originally meaning “plug” or “wad”.
Traditional tacos use beef, but chicken, pork, and turkey are also common.
Mexico boasts over 200 regional variations of taco fillings.
Tacos without cheese are often served with lime, salsa, and guacamole for bright acidity and creaminess.
Tacos gained widespread popularity in the United States in the 1920s through Mexican eateries and food trucks.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: The meat provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Beef contains heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat is rich in vitamin B12 and niacin, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Lactose‑free
items.content: Without cheese, this taco is suitable for people with lactose intolerance.

items.title: Fiber from vegetables
items.content: Fresh toppings like tomatoes, onions, and lettuce add dietary fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Salsa and pre‑made seasoning mixes can be salty; individuals with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Meat fat
items.content: Fatty cuts of beef increase the calorie load; opting for lean cuts is recommended.

items.title: Spice allergies
items.content: Some people may be allergic to chilies, cumin, or other spices used in the seasoning.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Meat must be cooked thoroughly to prevent salmonella and other food‑borne illnesses.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve tacos hot, folding the tortilla in half and filling it with meat, vegetables, salsa, and a squeeze of lime. Optional toppings include guacamole or lactose‑free sour cream.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared tacos are best eaten immediately. If needed, store the meat filling in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Tortillas should be kept in a dry place, sealed to retain crispness.
